clue.text: Passed round communists, reactionary and twisted

indicators.note: round says the dead word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: passed, as in passed away, means died

indicators.note: reactionary is taken as going backwards, so the communists word is read in reverse

parts.note: Trots is short for Trotskyists, a breed of communist

explanation.surface: Someone who died surrounded by hardline communists is described as reactionary and warped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reactionary' looks like a political label beside 'communists' but signals reading backwards, giving STORT; Trots is a common British nickname for Trotskyists.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bent out of shape or misrepresented is twisted; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Exercise monkey but not man

indicators.note: but not says the following word is taken away from the monkey

parts.note: the mandrill is a large West African monkey with a colourful face
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to exercise like a monkey, but not like a human.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking MAN off the front of MANDRILL leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Military or classroom training by repetition is a drill, a kind of exercise.

clue.text: Mocking report that's highly sexed

indicators.note: report signals that the word is heard rather than read, giving a soundalike spelling

parts.note: satirical writing mocks its targets, so mocking means satiric

explanation.surface: A mocking account that happens to be very sexual in content.
explanation.walkthrough: A satyr is a lustful woodland creature of Greek myth, so the adjective from it means lecherous.
explanation.definitionFit: Satyrs were famed for lust, so the adjective formed from them describes someone lecherous.

clue.text: Scary creatures arising from lesser gods

indicators.note: arising says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Frightening beings emerging from minor deities of mythology.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'arising' means reading upwards: SERGO sits inside 'lesser gods' and reads the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairy-tale giants who eat people are classic examples of frightening monsters.

clue.text: Teaching only half 20s China

indicators.note: only half says just the first four of the eight letters of the word are used

parts.note: refers to the answer at 20 down, which means raise; the plural gives a word for raises

explanation.surface: Teaching only half of the 1920s history of China.
explanation.walkthrough: '20s' looks like a decade but points to 20 down, whose answer means 'up', so 20s gives UPS. China is porcelain, not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcelain crockery is called china, and cups for tea are typical pieces of it.

clue.text: Suffering indigestion when extremely dirty and contaminated apple core eaten

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extreme letters, first and last, of the word
eaten says the central letter is swallowed inside the contaminated word

parts.note: an infected or contaminated wound is septic

indicators.note: the core of the fruit word is its central letter

explanation.surface: Someone gets indigestion after eating a filthy, tainted apple core.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eaten' looks like part of the apple story, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspepsia is the medical word for indigestion, so its adjective describes a sufferer.

clue.text: Put money away but deliver fancy vase

definitions.meaning: to put money aside for later
to rescue or deliver from harm

indicators.note: fancy here means elaborately reworked, so the letters of vase are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bank some cash, or hand over an ornate vase.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions and an anagram in one clue: 'Put money away', 'deliver' (as in deliver us from evil) and the letters of vase rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: to keep money aside, and to rescue someone from danger.

clue.text: Champion trail around the poles

indicators.note: around says the trail word goes about the poles

parts.note: spoor is the track or scent trail of an animal
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: A champion's trail circles both of the earth's poles.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause is to back it, which is what a supporter or backer does.

clue.text: Unofficial law enforcer poet from Rome right away topped one from Florence

indicators.note: right is abbreviated R, and away says that letter is removed

parts.note: Virgil, author of the Aeneid, was a Roman poet

indicators.note: topped means the head is cut off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: Dante Alighieri, author of the Divine Comedy, was a Florentine

explanation.surface: A self-appointed lawman beheads a Florentine after a Roman poet loses his right.
explanation.walkthrough: VIRGIL without R gives VIGIL; DANTE without its top letter gives ANTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who takes the law into their own hands without authority is a self-appointed enforcer.

clue.text: Winner by a nose: pig out on this?

definitions.text: Winner by a nose: pig out on this?

parts.words: Winner by a nose: pig out on this?
parts.note: a victor plus a light porous thing, read as a cake one might gorge on

explanation.surface: A racing photo-finish and a binge on the celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: The winner is a victor and the cake is named after Queen Victoria; a sponge soaks things up as a glutton does.
explanation.definitionFit: This jam-filled layer cake, named after a queen, is the kind of treat people overindulge on.

clue.text: See 8
Slight addendum for drinks

parts.note: a slight is an insult, as is a slur
PS, postscript, is an addendum to a letter

explanation.surface: A small afterthought added to a list of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To drink noisily is to slurp; as a verb in the third person it fits drinks.

clue.text: Tools that could make us listen

indicators.note: could make says the letters of the following words can be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Implements that might force us to pay attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitchen implements and other handheld instruments are utensils, a synonym for tools.

clue.text: It makes you sick to see ice cap melting

indicators.note: melting means the ice cap loses its shape, so its letters are reformed

explanation.surface: Watching a polar ice cap melt is sickening.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipecacuanha syrup is a plant-based emetic used to induce vomiting.

clue.text: Primarily people of rank artist represented here

definitions.text: Primarily people of rank artist represented here

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of each of the next three words
represented here means re-presented, the letters of artist set out afresh

explanation.surface: Pictures of aristocrats painted by an artist are shown in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: POR, the initials of 'people of rank', joins TRAITS, from rearranging artist. The whole clue describes the paintings too.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintings of nobility done by an artist are likenesses of people, the pictures this clue describes.

clue.text: See 22 down
Augustus returns to besiege Italian city, as sewers working

indicators.note: to besiege means to surround, so the reversed name goes around the city
returns says the short name is read backwards

parts.note: Gus is a short form of the name Augustus
Turin is a city in northern Italy

explanation.surface: An emperor comes back to lay siege to an Italian city while drains operate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewers' means people who sew, not drains; 'returns' gives SUG, and Augustus is not the emperor but a full form of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons stitching up a wound are sewing, which is the act of stitching closed.

clue.text: Very French to approve sin

parts.note: tres is French for very
to pass a bill or plan is to approve it

explanation.surface: A very French attitude of giving sin the nod.
explanation.definitionFit: In the biblical sense, as in the Lord's Prayer, a trespass is a wrongdoing.

clue.text: See 19
Most blue West End seats not left first

indicators.note: first says the trimmed seats word comes before the other piece
not says the left letter is left out of the seats word

parts.note: saddles are seats on horses and bicycles

indicators.note: End asks for the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: The most depressing seats in London's West End theatres.
explanation.walkthrough: SADDLES without L gives SADDES, then T, the end of West. The West End is London's theatre district, but here it means the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue means sad or low in spirits, so the superlative of it is the gloomiest.

clue.text: Quiz programme ends with: "Set up secret recipe for pancakes"

indicators.note: a recipe is a way of mixing ingredients, so the letters are mixed together
ends asks for the final letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A TV quiz show closes with a secret pancake recipe being arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: ZE (the ends of 'Quiz programme') goes into the mix with the letters of 'Set up secret'.
explanation.definitionFit: This French dessert is thin pancakes in an orange and liqueur sauce, often flambéed.

clue.text: Up at 11, almost out

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their order and rearranged
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: eleven written out as a word

explanation.surface: Getting up at eleven, nearly late and out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: ELEVEN loses its last letter under 'almost', giving ELEVE, which 'out' rearranges with AT.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something or lift it higher is to up it, so up as a verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Sprinkled on the middle of pizzas left parched outside

indicators.note: outside says the parched word goes around the others

parts.note: parched means dried up

indicators.note: the middle of picks out the central letters of the word

explanation.surface: Topping sprinkled on pizzas that have been left to dry out.
explanation.definitionFit: Pouring oil or icing in a thin stream is drizzling it, much like a light sprinkling.

clue.text: Scrambled egg in a biological process

indicators.note: scrambled, as with eggs, means mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Scrambling an egg as a biological process.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing older is a natural process all living things go through over time.

clue.text: Strange place, with pet eating tart for dessert

indicators.note: eating says the rearranged letters swallow the tart word
strange signals the letters are put into an odd new order

parts.note: tart is slang for a prostitute, as is harlot

explanation.surface: An odd place where a pet scoffs a tart for pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of place and pet are rearranged around HARLOT. 'tart' wants to be a pastry, but here it is a loose woman.
explanation.definitionFit: This baked pudding of stewed fruit in a bread or sponge case is a classic dessert.

clue.text: Curious about Philistine being rowdy

indicators.note: about says the curious word goes around the setter

parts.note: nosy means inquisitive or curious
the setter's pseudonym, so it means me, the letter I

explanation.surface: An inquisitive person asks about a boorish individual behaving raucously.
explanation.walkthrough: Philistine is this puzzle's setter, so the setter's name stands for I.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowdy crowd makes a racket, so loud and boisterous fit as synonyms.

clue.text: Richard heard of cheap goods order

indicators.note: heard signals the name is taken by its sound, with a different spelling

parts.note: Dick is a pet form of Richard
tat is cheap, shoddy merchandise

explanation.surface: Richard hears about an order for cheap goods.
explanation.walkthrough: TAT is British slang for tacky, cheap goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A diktat is a decree imposed without consultation, a high-handed command.

clue.text: By stripping, tempt that jerk to become forceful

indicators.note: stripping takes off the outer letters of each of the two words, leaving the middles

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary jerk or twitch

explanation.surface: Tempting a jerk into stripping, forcefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripping' looks like undressing, but it strips the outer letters off both words.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphatic speech is delivered with force and emphasis, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Man possibly read out passage

indicators.note: read out signals the word is spoken, giving a soundalike spelling

parts.note: an aisle is a passage between rows of seats

explanation.surface: A man perhaps reading a passage out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is not a person but the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea, so Man is one example.

clue.text: Axes elm tree that's crooked to a large extent

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the x and y axes of a graph, so the letters X and Y

explanation.surface: Axes cut down an elm tree that has grown bent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axes' looks like chopping tools but means the x and y axes of a graph.
explanation.definitionFit: Extremely means very greatly or in a high degree, matching to a large extent.
